meta.title: The Hidden Treasure and the Pearl
meta.verseText: May your kingdom come. May what you want to happen be done on earth as it is done in heaven.
meta.theme: God's kingdom is the greatest treasure of all, worth more than everything else.

questions.text: Who told the stories about the hidden treasure and the pearl?
questions.hint: He used short, simple stories called parables.
questions.explanation: Jesus told the parables of the hidden treasure and the pearl to help people understand God's kingdom.

questions.text: Where did the man find the hidden treasure?
questions.hint: Families sometimes buried valuables there to keep them safe.
questions.explanation: In Matthew 13:44, the man found the treasure hidden in a field.

questions.text: What did the man do after he found the treasure in the field?
options: He joyfully sold everything to buy the field
He gave it to the king
questions.hint: He was filled with joy and gave up everything else.
questions.explanation: The man joyfully sold all he had to buy the field, because the treasure was worth far more.

questions.text: What special item was the merchant looking for?
questions.hint: It comes from inside an oyster.
questions.explanation: The merchant was searching for fine pearls and found one extraordinary pearl.

questions.text: What did the merchant do when he found the one very valuable pearl?
options: He sold everything he had to buy it
He traded one pearl for it
He decided not to buy it
questions.hint: He gave up all his other pearls and possessions.
questions.explanation: The merchant sold everything he owned to buy the one pearl of great value.

questions.text: What is a parable?
options: A short, simple story that teaches a lesson
questions.hint: Jesus used everyday life to teach big truths.
questions.explanation: A parable is a short, simple story from everyday life that Jesus used to teach about God's kingdom.

questions.text: Both the treasure and the pearl stories teach us that God's kingdom is worth more than everything else.
questions.hint: Both men gave up everything they had.
questions.explanation: True. In both parables, the people gave up everything because God's kingdom is the greatest treasure.

questions.text: What were Peter and Andrew doing when Jesus called them?
questions.hint: They worked on the water and used nets.
questions.explanation: In Matthew 4:18, Peter and Andrew were fishermen casting their nets into the sea.

questions.text: How quickly did the first disciples follow Jesus when He called them?
questions.hint: The Bible says they left their nets immediately.
questions.explanation: The disciples left their nets at once and followed Jesus right away.

questions.text: James and John left their boat and their _____ to follow Jesus.
questions.hint: He was the man who taught them to fish.
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:22 says they left the boat and their father and followed Jesus.

questions.text: Fill in the blank: 'Loving God and His kingdom is most _____!'
questions.hint: This is the Bottom Line of the lesson.
questions.explanation: The Bottom Line is 'Loving God and His kingdom is most important!'

questions.text: Why did the man sell everything to buy the field?
options: The treasure was worth so much more
He was told to by a king
He needed a new field to farm
questions.hint: It wasn't because his other things were bad.
questions.explanation: He sold everything not because his things were worthless, but because the treasure was worth far more.

questions.text: What did many people wrongly think God's kingdom would be like?
options: Power, force, or a political takeover
questions.hint: Some expected a warrior king.
questions.explanation: Many thought God's kingdom meant power, force, a warrior king, or a political takeover, but Jesus showed it was something greater.

questions.text: The disciples followed Jesus because they were running away from their boring lives.
questions.hint: They saw something worth MORE, not something to escape.
questions.explanation: False. The disciples weren't running away; they saw something better in Jesus worth leaving everything for.

questions.text: In the parables, what happens when someone realizes something has more value than everything else?
options: Their priorities shift and decisions become clear
questions.hint: Think about what changes inside the person.
questions.explanation: When people see the greatest value, their priorities rearrange and the right choice becomes clear, like with God's kingdom.

questions.text: What is the memory verse asking God for?
options: For His kingdom to come and His will to be done
questions.hint: It's about God's kingdom coming to earth.
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:10 asks for God's kingdom to come and His will to be done on earth as in heaven.

questions.text: Fill in the blank: 'May your _____ come. May what you want to happen be done on earth as it is done in heaven.'
questions.hint: It's what the whole lesson is about.
questions.explanation: The memory verse, Matthew 6:10, says 'May your kingdom come.'

questions.text: How can you make God's kingdom most important in your life?
options: By putting God first and letting everything else fall into place
questions.hint: God becomes the center, not just an add-on.
questions.explanation: We make God's kingdom the center of our lives so everything else falls into place around Him.

questions.text: When you understand how good God is, it changes how you see everything else.
questions.hint: Seeing the greatest treasure changes your view.
questions.explanation: True. Seeing how good God is and how amazing His kingdom is changes how we view everything.

questions.text: What is a good question to ask yourself from this lesson?
options: What actually comes first in my life?
How many toys do I have?
questions.hint: It's about what matters most.
questions.explanation: The Conversation Starter invites us to ask, 'What actually comes first in my life?'

questions.text: Does loving God's kingdom mean other good things in life stop mattering?
options: No, but God becomes most important and helps everything else fall into place
Yes, you must give away all toys
questions.hint: The lesson says other things aren't bad.
questions.explanation: Other good things still matter, but God's kingdom becomes the center that puts everything in the right place.

questions.text: Which Bible book contains the stories of the hidden treasure and the pearl?
questions.hint: It's the first book of the New Testament.
questions.explanation: The parables are found in Matthew 13:44-46.

questions.text: How did the man feel when he found the hidden treasure?
questions.hint: The Bible says he did it 'joyfully.'
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:44 says the man joyfully sold all he had to buy the field.

questions.text: Crowds gathered to listen to Jesus because they wanted to understand what God's kingdom is really like.
questions.hint: All kinds of people came to hear Him.
questions.explanation: True. Crowds of all kinds of people gathered, wanting to understand God's kingdom.

questions.text: Fill in the blank: Jesus used _____ to help people understand something as big as God's kingdom.
questions.hint: Short, simple stories from everyday life.
questions.explanation: Jesus used parables, simple everyday stories, to teach about God's kingdom.

questions.text: What did the disciples' lives revolve around before they followed Jesus?
questions.hint: They were fishermen.
questions.explanation: Their whole world was built around their nets, jobs, skills, and security as fishermen.

questions.text: If a friend wanted to follow Jesus but was nervous to give up something, what would help them?
options: Telling them God's kingdom is worth more than anything
Telling them to keep it a secret
Telling them to wait until they are grown up
questions.hint: Remember why the man and merchant gladly gave things up.
questions.explanation: Like the man and merchant, knowing God's kingdom is worth more than anything helps us follow Jesus with joy.

questions.text: The hidden treasure and the pearl are pictures of how valuable God's kingdom is.
questions.hint: Both stories point to the same big idea.
questions.explanation: True. Both the treasure and the pearl show that God's kingdom is the most valuable thing of all.

questions.text: Fill in the blank: The disciples 'at once left their _____ and followed him.'
questions.hint: It's the tool fishermen use.
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:20 says they at once left their nets and followed Jesus.

questions.text: What does it mean that God's kingdom becomes 'the center' of your life?
options: You only go to church on holidays
God is the most important thing and shapes everything else
questions.hint: Not just added to a list, but at the heart.
questions.explanation: Making God the center means He is most important and helps everything else in life fall into place.

questions.text: Which two brothers were the first fishermen Jesus called?
questions.hint: They were casting nets into the sea.
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:18 says Jesus first called Peter (Simon) and his brother Andrew.

questions.text: What can you do this week to put God first, like the people in the stories?
options: Pray and choose to love God most
questions.hint: Think about a simple way to make God most important.
questions.explanation: We can pray and choose each day to love God and His kingdom most, just like the man, merchant, and disciples.

story.summary: Jesus told two short stories to help people understand how valuable God's kingdom is. A man found treasure hidden in a field and joyfully sold everything he had to buy that field. A merchant searching for fine pearls found one perfect pearl and sold all he owned to buy it. Both gave up everything because they had found something worth far more. Jesus showed this was real when He called four fishermen, Peter, Andrew, James, and John. They left their nets, boats, and even their father at once to follow Him, because they saw that Jesus and God's kingdom were worth more than anything. The lesson reminds us that loving God and His kingdom is most important of all.

scenes.title: The Crowds Gather
scenes.description: All kinds of people gathered around Jesus, wanting to understand what God's kingdom is really like. Some thought it meant power or a warrior king. So Jesus began to teach them using parables, simple stories from everyday life.

scenes.title: The Hidden Treasure
scenes.description: Jesus told about a man who found treasure buried in a field. Filled with joy, the man sold everything he had to buy that field, not because his things were bad, but because the treasure was worth so much more.

scenes.title: The Priceless Pearl
scenes.description: Jesus told about a merchant searching for fine pearls. When he found one extraordinary pearl, he sold everything he owned to buy it. God's kingdom is like that pearl, worth more than everything else.

scenes.title: Jesus Calls the Fishermen
scenes.description: Jesus walked by the sea and called Peter and Andrew, then James and John. At once they left their nets, their boat, and their father to follow Him, because they saw that following Jesus was worth more than everything.

scenes.title: What Matters Most
scenes.description: Like the man, the merchant, and the disciples, we can see that God's kingdom is the greatest treasure. When we put God first, everything else falls into place. Loving God and His kingdom is most important!
